topic: Modern multitasking actually reduces your brain's capacity for deep focus
subject: society

facts.claim: In a study on pain distraction, participants in the distraction group reported significantly less pain, but the pain experience was not influenced by executive functioning abilities.
facts.quote: Participants in the distraction group reported significantly less pain during the CPT, but the pain experience was not influenced by executive functioning abilities.

facts.claim: PFC volume is linked to stronger executive performance in older samples, but this is unrelated to the mean age of a sample.
facts.quote: Stronger associations between executive functions and PFC volume were linked to greater variance in the sample age but was unrelated to the mean age of a sample.

facts.claim: Subjective cognitive function can predict objective performance on some executive function tasks, but there was not definitive evidence regarding switching.
facts.quote: This suggests that subjective cognitive function can predict objective performance on at least some executive function tasks. We discuss methodological and theoretical factors that constrain the maximum observable correlation and consider the relative insights that subjective measures versus task performance provide.

facts.claim: Ecstasy users showed significant performance deficits in switching (SMD = -0.19, 95% CI -0.36 to -0.02, Z = 2.16, p < 0.05, I 2 = 85%).
facts.quote: Ecstasy users showed significant performance deficits in access (SMD = -0. 33, 95% CI -0. 46 to -0. 19, Z = 4. 72, p < 0. 001, I 2 = 74%), switching (SMD = -0. 19, 95% CI -0. 36 to -0. 02, Z = 2. 16, p < 0. 05, I 2 = 85%) and updating (SMD = -0. 26, 95% CI -0. 37 to -0. 15, Z = 4. 49, p < 0. 001, I 2 = 82%).

facts.claim: High math anxiety was associated with disengagement from math trials and reduced neural activity in regions associated with arithmetic processing when switching from a control task.
facts.quote: When switching from the control task, high math anxiety (HMA) was associated with disengagement from math trials, speeding through these trials, and exhibiting reduced neural activity in regions associated with arithmetic processing.

facts.claim: Larger prefrontal cortex (PFC) volume and greater PFC thickness are linked to better executive performance in healthy adults.
facts.quote: We found that larger PFC volume and greater PFC thickness were associated with better executive performance.

research.angle: While larger prefrontal cortex volume is linked to better executive performance, evidence shows that task switching can be associated with disengagement and reduced neural activity in specific contexts like math anxiety.
research.verdict: The sources show that prefrontal cortex volume relates to executive function and that switching can lead to neural disengagement, but they do not directly measure how rapid task-switching degrades the prefrontal cortex's efficiency in a general multitasking context.
research.caveat: The studies provided focus on specific conditions like drug use, math anxiety, and pain distraction rather than general modern multitasking.
